title: Kimi K3 Inference Benchmark on DGX-B300
gist: An outside benchmark of Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, on one eight-GPU B300 node. It runs vLLM and SGLang, each with and without the drafter their official recipes recommend, from 1 to 64 concurrent requests. Speculation nearly doubles one user's speed, breaks even at 16 concurrent in vLLM and 4 in SGLang, and at 64 delivers less than half the tokens of plain decoding.
changes: The first measured mixture-of-experts table, and it fades like the dense ones. The rising curve a cost model predicted for such models has not shown up in a real engine. It also shows the engines' recipes fix the draft length, which at 64 concurrent cost more than half the throughput.
caveats: One model, one node, 128-token prompts and answers, template prompts, and a fixed draft of seven tokens. The speculative vLLM run capped running requests at 32, which alone could flatten its curve past 32; the break-even at 16 sits below that cap. The two engines used different drafters. Measured by a hardware reseller. Spreading the model over eight GPUs may hide the small-batch expert effect.

numbers.metric: Per-user speed with speculation, one request

bears_on.note: Whether to speculate flips with the load and with the engine: on one model and chip, break-even came at 16 concurrent in vLLM and 4 in SGLang.
